question: A, B, C, E, F, P, and Q are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. Only four people sit between C and E, when counted from the right of C. C sits third to the left of P. B sits third to the left of F. Q is an immediate neighbour of both E and P. How many people sit between A and Q, when counted from the right of A?
solution:
Given:

A, B, C, E, F, P, and Q are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

Only four people sit between C and E, when counted from the right of C.

C sits third to the left of P.

Q is an immediate neighbour of both E and P. 

B sits third to the left of F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e06445ee0d97ba75cc712557c824f3c465a50ce668d5b8bc7bbca2449ccb2fca.png] 

Thus, two people sit between A and Q, when counted from the right of A.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option1 ".**
